clue.text: Unmoved by flashes on the screen

explanation.surface: Someone sits unmoved by flickering images on a television screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Static means motionless, and static is also the speckled interference that crackles across a TV picture.

clue.text: Dictionary of Latin law pore over

parts.note: lex is the Latin word for law
to con is to study or pore over a text closely

explanation.surface: A student studies a dictionary of Roman legal terms.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan text lost the single word 'I'; the clue reads 'Dictionary of Latin law I pore over'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lexicon is a word book, the vocabulary of a language set out in order, which is what a dictionary is.

clue.text: Brief message from those C torn asunder

indicators.note: torn asunder means ripped apart, so the letters of the words before are pulled about and reassembled

explanation.surface: A short letter has been ripped in half by those who received it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'asunder' shuffles the nine letters of THOSE and TORN. 'torn' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A short note is a quick written message of a few lines.

clue.text: More than one story 1 finds moving

indicators.note: moving means the letters of the referenced answer are set in motion and rearranged

parts.note: the numeral points at the answer to 1 down, used here as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A reader finds a series of tales emotionally moving.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue borrows the answer to 1 down, STATIC, and 'moving' rearranges it; static versus moving is the setter's pairing. 'story' is the floor of a building, not a tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Attics are rooms on the top floor of a house, so several of them are more than one storey.

clue.text: Local drink record held in Derbyshire

definitions.note: the definition is a place, a town located in that county

indicators.note: held means the record is gripped inside the drink

parts.note: beer is the drink of the local, the British word for a neighbourhood pub
LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A pub's beer and a gramophone record are kept somewhere in Derbyshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held' sets the record inside the drink. 'Local' is British slang for one's nearby pub; Derbyshire is a county in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Belper is a mill town in the Derwent valley of that county.

clue.text: Her rank prohibits one's admission

indicators.note: admission means letting in, so one's is let inside the word for prohibits

parts.note: bars means forbids or prohibits
taken as written, ONE'S without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A woman of rank refuses to let someone enter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admission' lets the words for one's in; 'Her' is part of the definition, a woman's rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A baroness is a woman holding the lowest title of the peerage, so it is a female rank.

clue.text: Tweedy shade much seen around Virginia

indicators.note: around means the word for much encircles the state abbreviation

parts.note: a lot means much
VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: A tweed colour is commonly worn across the state of Virginia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' wraps much round the state; 'seen' is a link. Lovat is a Scottish tweed colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovat is a muted green or blue-grey mix typical of Scottish tweeds.

clue.text: Settle comfortably in Amiens, conceivably

indicators.note: in means the letters lie inside the run of words that follows, across the comma

explanation.surface: Someone may well make themselves at home in the French city of Amiens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points into AmiENS CONCEivably.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensconce oneself is to settle snugly and securely in a place.

clue.text: Drivers take eighteen of them as a matter of course

definitions.text: Drivers take eighteen of them as a matter of course

parts.words: Drivers take eighteen of them as a matter of course
parts.note: drivers here are golf clubs, and a course is a golf course of eighteen holes, each begun from a tee

explanation.surface: Motorists routinely take eighteen of something on their journeys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drivers' suggests motorists and 'course' a routine, but these are golf terms: a round of eighteen holes starts each hole with a drive from the tee.
explanation.definitionFit: Each hole on a golf course opens with a drive from the teeing ground, so a round has eighteen of them.

clue.text: Most daring pair of undergarments

parts.note: a bra is one undergarment
a vest is a second undergarment, a sleeveless one worn under a shirt in Britain

explanation.surface: The boldest outfit is just a couple of pieces of underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pair of undergarments' gives two items, BRA and VEST; in Britain a vest is an undershirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravest is the superlative of brave, so it means boldest or most daring.

clue.text: Juryman in Marx's birthplace

explanation.surface: A member of a jury in the town where Karl Marx was born.
explanation.definitionFit: A trier is someone who tries a case, as jurors do, and Trier is the German city on the Moselle where Karl Marx was born.

clue.text: Motor race bloomer

parts.note: a motor is a car
a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: A motor race ends in a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a blunder but means a flowering plant; 'race' is an ethnic people, not a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A carnation is a garden flower, so it is a plant that blooms.

clue.text: Request from Saskatchewan

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the place name that follows

explanation.surface: A petition arrives from the Canadian province of Saskatchewan.
explanation.walkthrough: The province name is a Canadian prairie province; the word sits just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking is how one puts in a request, so the verb and the noun's action are the same thing.

clue.text: Indifference to Noel's predicament in a Greek island

indicators.note: in means the scrambled name sits inside the island

parts.note: Cos (Kos) is a Greek island in the Dodecanese

indicators.note: a predicament is a mess or fix, so the letters of the name are put into disorder

explanation.surface: Noel is unmoved by the trouble he finds himself in on a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'predicament' scrambles the name and 'in' sets the result inside the island; Cos is also spelt Kos.
explanation.definitionFit: Coolness is a calm lack of interest or warmth, which is indifference.

clue.text: Well-groomed tree

explanation.surface: A neatly trimmed tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Spruce means neat and smart in appearance, and a spruce is an evergreen conifer.

clue.text: Afflict with colour quaintly pleasing

parts.note: perse is an old-fashioned word for a dark greyish-blue colour, and quaintly marks it as archaic
cute means attractive or pleasing

explanation.surface: Someone is troubled by an old-fashioned but charming colour scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quaintly' tells you the colour word is archaic: perse, a deep blue-grey found in old texts.
explanation.definitionFit: To persecute is to harass or torment, so it means to afflict someone persistently.

clue.text: So long in France

parts.note: so long is an informal farewell, and the clue asks for the French way of saying it

explanation.surface: A long stay in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So long' reads as a length of time but is a goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means until we see each other again, the everyday French goodbye.

clue.text: Fly from a mixed double set

indicators.note: mixed means the letters of the doubled word are rearranged, as partners are in mixed doubles
double means the word set is taken twice

explanation.surface: A tennis set of mixed doubles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double' gives SETSET and 'mixed' rearranges it; the surface is tennis, with mixed doubles and a set.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsetse is an African fly that spreads sleeping sickness.

clue.text: Creature for whom living is a great drain

definitions.text: Creature for whom living is a great drain

parts.words: Creature for whom living is a great drain
parts.note: a great drain reads as a heavy burden, but here it is a large sewer where the animal makes its home

explanation.surface: Some poor creature finds that simply staying alive is exhausting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a great drain' sounds like a burden on resources; it is a literal big drain, the animal's habitat.
explanation.definitionFit: The brown rat is often called this because it lives in underground drains and sewers.

clue.text: See 17
City on mouse-coloured river

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown, the colour of a mouse
the Dee is a river in Scotland (and another in Wales and England)

explanation.surface: A city stands beside a grey-brown river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a Scottish river flowing to the sea at Aberdeen; the city in question is on the Tay.
explanation.definitionFit: Dundee is a city on the east coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Catch a number on the re- C rebound

indicators.note: a rebound bounces back, so the number is read in the opposite direction
this word means the letters it governs are turned round, so they are read backwards

parts.note: ten is a number

explanation.surface: A fielder catches the ball as it bounces back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rebound' turns TEN back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A net is a mesh for catching fish or animals, and to net something is to catch it.

clue.text: Not for profit in a way

indicators.note: in means profit sits inside the letters for a way

parts.note: A plus ST, the abbreviation for street, a kind of way
gain means profit

explanation.surface: A non-profit organisation working in a certain manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' splits the way, read as A plus street; 'Not for profit' looks like one phrase but the definition is only 'Not for'.
explanation.definitionFit: Against is the opposite of in favour of, so it means not for.

clue.text: Natural gift? Yes, in a certain number

indicators.note: in means the word yes sits inside the number

parts.note: eight is a specific number

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a talent is innate and is told yes, in some quantity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the word yes within the number; the question mark marks sight as a gift of nature.
explanation.definitionFit: Sight is one of the senses we are born with, a faculty given by nature.

clue.text: Worry reflected about a Scottish flower

definitions.note: a flower here is something that flows, a river in Scotland

indicators.note: about means the turned word goes around the letter a
reflected means the word is turned round as in a mirror

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A worried thought about a Scottish bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' turns WORRY into YRROW and 'about' wraps it round A. 'flower' is read as flow-er, a river: Yarrow Water flows in the Scottish Borders, and yarrow is also a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Yarrow Water is a river in the Scottish Borders, and a river is something that flows.

clue.text: There's little work in that headpiece

indicators.note: in means the short work sits inside the word that

parts.note: taken as written
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A hat that takes little effort to make.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' sets the opus inside the word that; 'There's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A top hat is a tall formal hat, a piece worn on the head.

clue.text: Object of Henry's devouring love!

annotationWithheld.why: 'Object of Henry's devouring love!' (9) for HENRIETTA: no parse found; the name is a feminine form of Henry, but 'devouring love' gives no letters or device I can account for, and no reprint or blog explains it

clue.text: Step upstairs

parts.note: reads as an order to go up, but describes the upright face of each stair in a flight

explanation.surface: An invitation to come up to the next floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Step upstairs' sounds like an instruction; it is a noun phrase for part of a staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: A riser is the vertical board between two treads of a staircase.

clue.text: Curl gives a mischief-maker little credit

parts.note: CR is the short form of credit in accounts
an imp is a mischievous sprite

explanation.surface: A naughty child earns a little praise for a curl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To crimp hair is to press it into small waves or curls.

clue.text: Associate with a swindling type?

parts.note: a con is a swindle
a sort is a type or kind

explanation.surface: Someone keeps company with a fraudster.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'swindling type' is split into two pieces rather than read as a con man.
explanation.definitionFit: To consort with someone is to keep their company or associate with them.

clue.text: Rebuilt houses at a town. near Portsmouth

indicators.note: rebuilt means the letters are taken down and put together again in a new order

explanation.surface: Houses being reconstructed in a town on the south coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rebuilt' rearranges HOUSES and AT. Portsmouth is a naval city on England's south coast; Southsea adjoins it.
explanation.definitionFit: Southsea is a seaside resort on Portsea Island, beside Portsmouth.

clue.text: Mount framing an artist in his element

indicators.note: framing means the element surrounds the artist like a picture frame

parts.note: art is the artist's natural element
A plus RA, a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A mountain is framed in a painting by an artist at his best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'framing' sets A plus RA (a Royal Academician) inside the artist's element; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ararat is the mountain in Turkey where Noah's ark came to rest.
